svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.10.16.1 Required Fire Blocks in Concealed Spaces
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.10.16.1 Required Fire Blocks in Concealed Spaces
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Required Fire Blocks in Concealed Spaces

g.text: Top plates block off the wall space below
Bottom plate and subfloor: the wall space above is
blocked off from the floor space. Sheathing cut away
Fire blocks where the wall space meets the space
in a drop ceiling, coved ceiling or soffit, where
exposed materials have a flame spread over 25
Fire blocks at the top and bottom of the run
where it passes through a floor with a concealed
space, exposed materials flame spread over 25
Unsprinklered attic: compartments not over 60 m
(196′-10¼″) in greatest dimension. With exposed materials
over 25 flame spread: 300 m² (3 229 ft²), 20 m (65′-7⅜″) max.

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
Vertical concealed spaces in interior walls and exterior walls are
separated by fire blocks
(a) one from the other, and (b) from horizontal concealed spaces.
Horizontal concealed spaces in attics, roof spaces, ceilings, floors
and crawl spaces are separated by fire blocks
(a) one from the other, and (b) from vertical concealed spaces.
Fire blocks at all interconnections between concealed vertical and
horizontal spaces in interior coved ceilings, drop ceilings and
soffits
Where the exposed construction materials within the concealed spaces have a
surface flame-spread rating greater than 25.
Fire blocks at the top and bottom of each run of stairs where they
pass through a floor containing concealed space
Where the exposed construction materials within the space have a surface
flame-spread rating greater than 25.
Where not sprinklered, concealed spaces of combustible construction
created by a ceiling, roof space or unoccupied attic space are
separated by fire blocks into compartments
(a) not more than 60 m (196′-10¼″) in greatest dimension, and (b) where the
space contains exposed construction materials with a surface flame-spread
rating greater than 25, not more than 300 m² (3 229 ft²) in area.
No dimension of the concealed space in Clause (5)(b) exceeds 20 m
Concealed spaces in mansard or gambrel style roofs, exterior cornices,
balconies and canopies of combustible construction have vertical fire
blocks
Where the exposed construction materials within the space have a surface
flame-spread rating exceeding 25: at intervals of not more than 20 m, and
where such spaces extend across the ends of required vertical fire
separations.
Drawn: framing cut away to show the concealed spaces. Red outlines: fire blocks. D is 40 m by 15 m.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.16.1. (page 9-92)
